I'll check the current styling for the WiFi card to fix the overflow issue that occurs at certain widths. Now I can see the issue. The `.wifi-name` class has a fixed font size that can cause the text to overflow at certain widths. I'll add proper word-breaking and overflow handling to ensure the WiFi network name stays within its container. Now let me rebuild the site to apply the changes: Perfect! I've fixed the WiFi network name overflow issue. The changes I made:

1. **Added `word-break: break-word`** - Allows long words to break and wrap to the next line
2. **Added `overflow-wrap: break-word`** - Ensures text wraps to prevent overflow
3. **Added `hyphens: auto`** - Enables automatic hyphenation for better text breaking (on desktop)

These properties are applied to both the regular `.wifi-name` style and the mobile media query version. Now the WiFi network name will automatically wrap and stay within its container at all screen widths, preventing the ugly overflow you were experiencing.
